name: Sable Mirage
specific_features: Satellite graveyard in a slow-decaying orbit
description: Sable Mirage is a small, airless world of black sand, its dust seas so dark they swallow starlight and leave the night side truly invisible. Solar wind has sculpted the dunes into rippled obsidian waves frozen mid-motion. A single enormous crater, floored with pale regolith, is the only landmark bright enough to navigate by.

There is no sound at all, no wind, no breath of atmosphere, only the crunch of boots on glassy grit and the creak of a suit in the violent thermal swing. Surface temperatures lurch from scorching to deep-freeze between sunrise and sunset. Underfoot, the low gravity makes every step a slow, floating bound across silence.

Long-range scans suggest the black dust is not native, as if the little world was coated by some ancient event no record survives to explain. In its decaying orbit drifts a graveyard of dead satellites from a dozen navies and eras, tumbling slowly over the terminator. Nobody has claimed them, and nobody has admitted to launching most of them.

Salvage crews prize the satellite graveyard for its intact cores and encrypted archives, though boarding derelicts in such fickle gravity has killed experienced spacers. The planet itself offers iron and silicon at prices that make marginal mining ventures tempting. But rumors persist that one of those satellites is still transmitting, faintly, on a frequency reserved for ships that went missing before the war.
